title: Healthcare Technology System Procurement
goal: Enable NHS organisations to systematically evaluate, select, and contract a clinical or administrative IT system that meets clinical, security, and compliance requirements
summary: A structured procurement process for healthcare IT systems — from business case through market scan, vendor evaluation, compliance review, and contract award. Applicable to EHR upgrades, clinical decision support tools, and administrative platforms requiring IG Toolkit compliance.

assumptions: Organisation is subject to NHS IG Toolkit and Data Security and Protection (DSP) requirements
A dedicated procurement lead and IT security officer are available

laneContent.description: Business need identified — current system end-of-life, new clinical capability required, or compliance gap discovered
IT Director works with clinical leads, compliance officer, and operations to document functional, technical, and regulatory requirements

channels.name: Stakeholder workshops
channels.usageContext: Requirements gathering with clinical and operational stakeholders

barriers.description: Clinical stakeholders struggle to articulate technical requirements in procurement language
DSP Toolkit requirements are not always known upfront — compliance officer involvement varies

laneContent.frontstage: Requirements specification document, stakeholder workshop sessions
laneContent.backstage: IT security review of mandatory compliance requirements, clinical governance sign-off on functional needs
design-opps: Create a healthcare-specific requirements template that embeds DSP Toolkit controls automatically
Provide a stakeholder interview guide for non-technical clinical leads

laneContent.description: Issue a Request for Information to known vendors and run independent market research to identify candidate solutions

channels.name: Find a Tender Service (FTS)
channels.usageContext: Issuing public RFI for above-threshold procurements

channels.name: G-Cloud / NHS Procurement frameworks
channels.usageContext: Identifying pre-approved vendors to reduce procurement overhead

barriers.description: Market is fragmented — it's hard to know which vendors have genuine NHS track records vs. generic SaaS pivoting to healthcare

laneContent.frontstage: RFI document, vendor questionnaire, market scan report
laneContent.backstage: Procurement team manages RFI responses, legal reviews NDA requirements
design-opps: Publish a healthcare IT vendor maturity index benchmarking DSP compliance, NHS interoperability, and implementation track record

laneContent.description: Evaluate RFI responses against scored criteria. Typically shortlists 3-5 vendors for full evaluation
laneContent.frontstage: Shortlist scoring matrix presented to procurement board
laneContent.backstage: IT and clinical leads score independently; scores reconciled in panel meeting

significance.description: First major gate — wrong shortlist selection propagates through the entire evaluation

laneContent.description: Shortlisted vendors present their solutions. Sessions include clinical workflow demonstrations, technical Q&A, and security discussions

channels.name: Video conference (Teams/Zoom)
channels.usageContext: Remote vendor demonstrations and follow-up Q&A

channels.name: Vendor premises or reference site visit
channels.usageContext: In-person system demonstration with reference customer

barriers.description: Vendors tailor demos to show strengths — evaluators need structured question banks to expose compliance gaps
Scheduling 5 vendors across a panel of 6 internal stakeholders takes weeks

laneContent.frontstage: Demo scripts, evaluation scorecards, live system demonstrations
laneContent.backstage: Security team prepares DSP Toolkit compliance question set; clinical governance team reviews clinical workflow mapping
support-systems: OWASP / NHS Cyber Security Framework question set
design-opps: Create a standardised NHS vendor demo script that forces vendors to address DSP controls in sequence

sla.targetDuration: Demos within 6 weeks of shortlist decision
sla.escalation: Escalate to CTO if any vendor fails to respond to demo scheduling within 5 working days

laneContent.description: IT security officer and data protection lead conduct a formal DSP Toolkit and cyber security assessment of preferred vendor(s)

channels.name: DSP Toolkit assessment portal
channels.usageContext: Formal compliance evidence submission and review

barriers.description: Vendors rarely have their DSP evidence pack pre-prepared — collection takes weeks and delays procurement timeline
NHS organisations often have only one data protection officer, creating a bottleneck

laneContent.frontstage: DSP Toolkit questionnaire responses, penetration test reports, data processing agreements
laneContent.backstage: IT security team reviews OWASP vulnerability disclosures, DPO reviews data flows and retention policies
design-opps: Create a vendor DSP readiness pre-check that can be shared before formal procurement begins, reducing audit cycle time

laneContent.description: Security officer presents findings. Decision: proceed, conditional approval (remediation required), or reject vendor
laneContent.frontstage: Security review report presented to procurement board
laneContent.backstage: IT security lead documents findings; DPO confirms data protection compliance

significance.description: Non-negotiable gate — a vendor that fails security cannot proceed regardless of clinical or commercial merit

laneContent.description: Calls with 2-3 NHS organisations already using the preferred vendor — focusing on implementation experience, support quality, and real-world DSP compliance

channels.name: Reference calls (peer NHS organisations)
channels.usageContext: Structured reference conversations with IT Directors at reference sites

barriers.description: Vendors only provide positive references — independent reference discovery through NHS networks is time-consuming

laneContent.frontstage: Reference call guide, reference site summary report
laneContent.backstage: Procurement lead identifies independent references via NHS Digital networks and peer contacts
design-opps: Build an NHS vendor reference database where IT Directors contribute post-implementation reviews

laneContent.description: IT Director synthesises evaluation findings into a board-ready business case: ROI, risk register, implementation timeline, and total cost of ownership

channels.name: Board presentation (PowerPoint/slides)
channels.usageContext: Presenting procurement recommendation to C-suite and board

barriers.description: Translating technical merit and compliance risk into financial terms that a non-technical CFO will approve is difficult

laneContent.frontstage: Business case document, ROI model, risk register
laneContent.backstage: Finance team reviews TCO model; clinical governance provides clinical benefit evidence
support-systems: NHS Green Book business case guidance
design-opps: Provide a healthcare IT business case template pre-populated with common ROI metrics and risk categories

laneContent.description: Business case submitted to board agenda. IT Director presents recommendation and answers questions

channels.name: Board or Executive Committee meeting
channels.usageContext: Formal procurement decision at executive level

barriers.description: Board meeting cycles (monthly or quarterly) create fixed decision windows — missing one cycle adds weeks of delay

laneContent.frontstage: Board agenda item, business case presentation
laneContent.backstage: CFO pre-reads and provides finance committee endorsement; CEO aligns with organisational strategy

significance.description: Final organisational commitment — approval triggers contract negotiation and resource allocation

laneContent.description: Board votes: approve, reject, or defer with conditions
laneContent.backstage: Company secretary records decision; procurement lead notified

laneContent.description: Legal and procurement teams negotiate contract terms: SLAs, data processing agreement, exit provisions, and implementation milestones

channels.name: Contract management platform
channels.usageContext: Redlined contract review and version management

barriers.description: Vendors often redline NHS standard terms, triggering multiple legal review cycles

laneContent.backstage: Legal team reviews redlines; DPO approves Data Processing Agreement; procurement finalises commercial terms
design-opps: Publish vendor-facing guidance on NHS standard contract expectations to reduce first-round redline volume

laneContent.description: Project formally begins. Governance structure established, project charter signed, and delivery plan agreed

channels.name: Project kickoff workshop
channels.usageContext: Establishing project governance and delivery plan

laneContent.frontstage: Project charter, delivery plan, RACI matrix
laneContent.backstage: PMO registers project; IT team allocates infrastructure capacity; vendor assigns implementation lead

significance.description: Transition from procurement to delivery — marks successful completion of the procurement process

laneContent.description: Contract signed, implementation underway, procurement process formally closed
Board rejects or defers procurement. Requirements review initiated for future re-tender

paths.name: Successful procurement
paths.description: First-pass shortlist, single security audit cycle, board approval at first submission

paths.name: Preferred vendor fails security — re-evaluate
paths.description: Security audit rejects preferred vendor; second-shortlist vendor progresses

paths.name: Board defers — revised business case required
paths.description: Board requests more information or cost reduction before approving

phases.name: Discovery and Requirements
phases.goal: Define what the organisation needs and why

phases.name: Detailed Evaluation
phases.goal: Assess shortlisted vendors across clinical, technical, and commercial dimensions

phases.name: Decision and Contract
phases.goal: Secure organisational approval and agree contract terms

researchSources.source: NHS Procurement Framework guidance and Find a Tender Service documentation
DSP Toolkit and NHS Cyber Security Framework requirements
Composite from NHS IT Director interviews (research personas)
